questions.q: In the messy export, what category of problem is "TX" vs. "Texas" in the State column?
options: Completeness
Uniqueness
Security
Consistency
questions.explain: Same real value, two different spellings — that's a consistency problem, fixed with formulas, picklists, or a lookup table.

questions.q: Why are "Acme Corp" and "acme corp " treated as a different kind of problem from the blank Email fields?
options: They're a likely-duplicate signal that needs human review, not just a formatting fix
They aren't different — both are completeness problems
Company name differences can never be cleaned with formulas
Blank fields are always more severe than casing differences
questions.explain: Two rows that look like the same real company, once cleaned, become a duplicate-management question — a human or duplicate rule should decide, not an automated merge.

questions.q: After applying TRIM(UPPER(...)) to the State column, why are "TX" and "TEXAS" still two different values?
options: The formula was applied to the wrong column
TRIM and UPPER cannot be used together in the same formula
UPPER and TRIM only standardize case and whitespace, not the underlying content
Salesforce ignores formula results on import
questions.explain: Case-normalizing formulas don't change what the text means — "tx" becomes "TX" and "Texas" becomes "TEXAS", which are still different strings needing a picklist or lookup table.

questions.q: Why shouldn't you invent a plausible email address to fill the blank Email fields before import?
options: Salesforce blocks all imports containing blank fields
It would trade a completeness problem for an accuracy problem, which is worse and harder to catch later
Email fields cannot be blank in a CSV file
Invented values are automatically flagged and rejected by Data Loader
questions.explain: A blank field is visibly incomplete and easy to find later. An invented but wrong value looks complete and accurate, making it much harder to catch and fix.

questions.q: After cleanup, rows for Acme Corp became character-for-character identical. What's the right next step?
options: Import both rows as separate Accounts to preserve history
Delete both rows since neither can be trusted anymore
Convert the Company field to a formula field
Let a duplicate rule catch the match at import/save time rather than importing both blindly
questions.explain: This is exactly the scenario duplicate rules exist for — catching the match and letting the configured action (block, alert, or report) decide what happens, instead of silently creating two records for one company.
